conventions.convention: A surface schema has two face-sides incident to each edge class and a single cyclic link at each vertex class. In a one-polygon word, opposite exponents are orientation compatible and equal exponents are twisted.
The sphere’s empty reduced word is notation only; its schema is the genuine digon aa⁻¹.
Complex forms use dzⱼ = dxⱼ + i dyⱼ and dbar zⱼ = dxⱼ − i dyⱼ; the dbar coefficient formula wedges dbar zⱼ before existing type factors.
Cauchy–Pompeiu uses outward-normal-first boundary orientation; its area form has coefficient −1/π when dA = dx∧dy.

A meromorphic differential changes expression by the coordinate derivative factor; its order is the Laurent order and its residue is the coefficient of the inverse first power in a centered coordinate. A nonconstant holomorphic map has local form z↦zᵉ, with e the ramification index.

The Jacobian matrix uses equation rows and coordinate columns. The curve-chart lemma extends that array convention to its local holomorphic functions without treating them as generators of a polynomial scheme ideal.

The Bochner–Martinelli formula uses the complex orientation dx₁∧dy₁∧…∧dxₙ∧dyₙ and the induced outward-normal-first boundary orientation; its statement assumes full AC and a bounded C¹ domain, not necessarily connected.

load_bearing.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Every nonempty compact connected boundaryless topological 2-manifold is homeomorphic to exactly one of the sphere, a connected sum of g≥1 tori, or a connected sum of k≥1 real projective planes. Two such surfaces are homeomorphic if and only if they have the same integral orientability and Euler characteristic.
For smooth complex-valued forms, d=∂+dbar, ∂²=0, dbar²=0, and ∂dbar+dbar∂=0; both operators satisfy the graded product rule with sign determined by total degree.
Assume AC. Every compact Riemann surface is canonically oriented by its holomorphic atlas and is homeomorphic to the sphere with exactly one handle number g≥0.
Assume AC. For a nonconstant holomorphic map f:X→Y between compact connected Riemann surfaces of degree d, the finite ramification sum satisfies 2g(X)−2=d(2g(Y)−2)+Σₓ(eₓ−1).

Assume AC. For bounded D⊂C with C¹ boundary, f∈C¹(cl D), and z∈D, outward-normal-first orientation gives f(z)=(1/(2πi))∫∂D f(ζ)/(ζ−z)dζ +(1/(2πi))∫D (∂̄f(ζ))/(ζ−z)dζ∧dbarζ; equivalently the area coefficient is −1/π.

Assume AC. On nested coordinate polydiscs, the stated parameterized one-variable transform is smooth, solves ∂̄ₖTₖg=g on the smaller polydisc, and preserves the other selected ∂̄ equations; for compactly supported smooth g on Cⁿ, the uncut transform is globally smooth and satisfies the corresponding derivative identities.

Assume AC and n≥2. Every smooth compactly supported dbar-closed (0,1)-form on Cⁿ has a unique smooth compactly supported solution u to dbar u=g, and u vanishes on the unique unbounded component of Cⁿ minus supp g.
Assume AC. For n≥1, a bounded open C¹ domain D⊂Cⁿ, f∈C¹(cl D), and z∈D, f(z)=∫∂D f(ζ)Ωₙ(ζ,z)−∫D dbarζ f(ζ)∧Ωₙ(ζ,z); the interior integral is absolutely convergent at ζ=z.

concerns.concern: In the anchor-density part of the proof, step 1.2 chooses a rational point q with |q−y|<ε/4 and then uses a(q), but the construction defines a(q) only for q in Q²∩D. The proof does not explicitly require q∈D. Since y∈D and D is open, choosing q sufficiently close also ensures q∈D, so this is a short proof-gap closure.

seams_checked.note: The curve-chart lemma uses the equation-row, coordinate-column Jacobian convention from the cited item. It expressly limits that item's polynomial-ideal scope and says its extension to local holomorphic functions is only an array convention; the Riemann page's use through the implicit function theorem does not strengthen the cited claim.

The Gauss–Bonnet page's related false statement is only that the curvature identity alone does not classify surfaces; its torus/Klein bottle comparison supports that limited claim and does not misstate the cited classification theorem.
